# Project overview  
This is a comprehensive informational website for PostgreSQL, an open-source object-relational database system. The site serves as the official public-facing platform for the PostgreSQL Global Development Group, providing detailed information about the software's features, history, community, and technical specifications. The tone is professional, technical, and informative, targeting developers, administrators, and organizations evaluating or using the database. The visual design is clean and structured, with a strong emphasis on content hierarchy and readability, using a consistent blue and white color scheme that reflects the brand identity.

The website is organized into a clear information architecture with distinct sections: a global navigation bar, a prominent hero area on the homepage, a left-hand sidebar for quick access to key topics, and a main content area that presents detailed text, lists, and statistics. The primary goal of the site is to educate users about PostgreSQL's capabilities, its robustness, and its extensive feature set, while also fostering community engagement through news, events, and user testimonials.

# Global structure and navigation  
The website features a consistent global shell across all pages, defined by a fixed header and footer. The header includes a large, stylized elephant logo (the PostgreSQL mascot) in the top-left corner, which acts as the home button. To the right of the logo is a search input field. Below this, a horizontal navigation bar contains links to the core sections: Home, About, Download, Documentation, Community, Developers, Support, Donate, and Your account. This navigation is persistent and appears at the top of every page.

A secondary navigation element is the "Quick Links" sidebar, located on the left side of the main content area on most pages. This sidebar provides a hierarchical list of key topics, including About, Governance, Policies, Feature Matrix, Donate, History, Sponsors, Latest News, Upcoming Events, Press, and Licence. It uses nested lists to show sub-items like "Contributing," "Financial," and "Servers" under Sponsors, and "Past events" under Upcoming Events.

The footer is consistent across all pages and contains a copyright notice ("Copyright © 1996-2026 The PostgreSQL Global Development Group") and a link trail at the bottom: "Policies | Code of Conduct | About PostgreSQL | Contact". The overall structure is designed for easy discovery of information, with a clear path from general navigation to specific details.

# Page-by-page requirements  

**index.html (desktop):**  
- **Hero Area:** A large banner featuring a gradient graphic of overlapping waves in shades of blue and green. The headline reads "PostgreSQL: The World's Most Advanced Open Source Relational Database." Below the headline is a call-to-action: "Download New to PostgreSQL?".
- **Main Content:** The page is divided into several distinct sections:
    - **New to PostgreSQL?:** An introductory paragraph followed by three buttons: "Learn More", "Feature Matrix", and "Governance".
    - **Latest Releases:** A section listing the latest versions (18.4, 17.10, etc.) with a brief description of the release notes. Includes a "Download" button and two smaller buttons: "Why Upgrade?" and "Security".
    - **Upcoming Events:** A list of events with dates, titles, and icons. Each event has a "Check Schedule" button and an "Add Your Event" button below the list.
    - **Mailing Lists:** A section explaining mailing lists with "Subscribe" and "View Archives" buttons.
    - **Learning Opportunities Ahead:** A section with "Browse Events" and "Browse User Groups" buttons.
    - **Latest News:** A list of recent blog posts with dates and authors.
    - **PLANET POSTGRES:** A feed of blog posts from the community, categorized by topic (e.g., Memories from PGConf.dev 2026, Twenty Years, Three CVEs, One AI).
    - **Seeing unexpected behavior?:** A section with a "Submit a Bug" button.

**about.html (desktop, tablet, mobile):**  
- **Header:** Identical to the index page, with the logo, search bar, and main navigation.
- **Shout Box:** A horizontal bar below the header announcing the latest release date and version numbers.
- **Sidebar:** A vertical "Quick Links" menu on the left, containing the same items as the global navigation but with more depth (e.g., "Sponsors" expands to "Contributing," "Financial," "Servers").
- **Main Content:** The primary content area is titled "About" with a small logo next to it. It contains the following sections:
    - **What is PostgreSQL?:** A descriptive paragraph explaining the database system.
    - **Why use PostgreSQL?:** A section detailing the benefits and features, broken down into categories like Data Types, Data Integrity, Concurrency, Performance, etc., each with a bulleted list of features.
    - **Any questions?:** A section directing users to documentation and community resources.
    - **Our users us:** A list of testimonials from various companies and individuals, each with a name, title, and company.
    - **What's a database project without statistics?:** A section presenting key metrics in a bold, large font format: "35+ Years Development", "725+ Contributors", "61,000+ Commits", "70+ Local User Groups", "1,780,000+ Lines of C", "720+ Events", "Millions of Happy Users", and "∞ Data Stored".

# Interaction and state requirements  

- **Navigation Menu:** The main navigation bar is a standard horizontal list. On mobile, the menu collapses into a hamburger icon (a toggle button). When clicked, it reveals the full list of navigation items in a dropdown. The toggle button itself is not interactive until clicked.
- **Search Functionality:** The search input field is a standard text box. Upon typing, it likely triggers a search query, though no specific UI feedback (like a loading spinner) is visible. The search button is a simple icon button.
- **Expandable Sections:** The "Quick Links" sidebar is static; there are no expandable/collapsible sections within it. However, the "Sponsors" and "Upcoming Events" items have sub-lists that are always visible.
- **Button States:** All buttons (e.g., "Download", "Subscribe", "Submit a Bug") are styled as solid rectangles with rounded corners. They do not change appearance on hover or click, indicating they are standard action buttons.
- **Form Submission:** The search form and the "Submit a Bug" form are standard HTML forms. There is no visible validation or error state shown in the provided images.
- **Content Expansion:** The "Latest Releases" section does not have any expandable content. The "Upcoming Events" list is static and does not allow for filtering or sorting.
- **User Flow:** The primary user flow is linear: navigate to a page via the main menu, read the content, and then use the sidebar or footer to navigate to related topics. The "Your account" link in the header suggests a potential login/registration flow, but no implementation details are visible.

# Responsive behavior  

- **Desktop:** The layout is wide and uses a two-column structure for the main content area. The "Quick Links" sidebar occupies the left column, and the main content occupies the right column. The header and footer remain fixed at the top and bottom.
- **Tablet:** The layout shifts to a single column. The "Quick Links" sidebar moves to the top of the page, directly below the header. The main content flows beneath it. The navigation menu remains horizontal but may be slightly condensed.
- **Mobile:** The layout is fully responsive. The navigation menu collapses into a hamburger icon. The "Quick Links" sidebar becomes a vertical stack below the header. The main content area stacks vertically, with all elements arranged in a single column. The hero section adjusts to fit the screen width, with text and buttons stacked vertically. All content blocks are displayed in a single column, ensuring readability on small screens.

# Visual language and content details  

- **Color Palette:** The primary colors are a deep blue (#336791) and a metallic gold (#e7eae8). These are used consistently for branding, buttons, and highlights. The background is primarily white or light gray.
- **Typography:** The font is a clean, sans-serif typeface. Headings are bold and large, while body text is clear and readable.
- **Imagery:** The PostgreSQL elephant logo is used extensively as a brand element. Abstract wave graphics in blue and green gradients are used in the hero sections.
- **Icons:** Font Awesome icons are used for various purposes, such as the magnifying glass for search and the hamburger menu icon.
- **Buttons:** Buttons are styled with rounded corners and use the primary blue or gold colors. They have a subtle hover effect.
- **Layout:** The site uses a grid-based layout with consistent spacing and alignment. Content blocks are clearly separated by white space.

About

What is PostgreSQL?

PostgreSQL is a powerful, open source object-relational database system that uses and extends the SQL language combined with many features that safely store and scale the most complicated data workloads. The origins of PostgreSQL date back to 1986 as part of the POSTGRES project at the University of California at Berkeley and has nearly 40 years of active development on the core platform.

PostgreSQL has earned a strong reputation for its proven architecture, reliability, data integrity, robust feature set, extensibility, and the dedication of the open source community behind the software to consistently deliver performant and innovative solutions. PostgreSQL runs on all major operating systems, has been ACID-compliant since 2001, and has powerful add-ons such as the popular PostGIS geospatial database extender. It is no surprise that PostgreSQL has become the open source relational database of choice for many people and organisations.

Getting started with using PostgreSQL has never been easier - pick a project you want to build, and let PostgreSQL safely and robustly store your data.

Why use PostgreSQL?

PostgreSQL comes with many features aimed to help developers build applications, administrators to protect data integrity and build fault-tolerant environments, and help you manage your data no matter how big or small the dataset. In addition to being free and open source, PostgreSQL is highly extensible. For example, you can define your own data types, build out custom functions, even write code from different programming languages without recompiling your database!

PostgreSQL tries to conform with the SQL standard where such conformance does not contradict traditional features or could lead to poor architectural decisions. Many of the features required by the SQL standard are supported, though sometimes with slightly differing syntax or function. Further moves towards conformance can be expected over time. As of the version 18 release in September 2025, PostgreSQL conforms to at least 170 of the 177 mandatory features for SQL:2023 Core conformance. As of this writing, no relational database meets full conformance with this standard.

Below is an inexhaustive list of various features found in PostgreSQL, with more being added in every major release:

  • Data Types
    • Primitives: Integer, Numeric, String, Boolean
    • Structured: Date/Time, Array, Range / Multirange, UUID
    • Document: JSON/JSONB, XML, Key-value (Hstore)
    • Geometry: Point, Line, Circle, Polygon
    • Customizations: Composite, Custom Types
  • Data Integrity
    • UNIQUE, NOT NULL
    • Primary Keys
    • Foreign Keys
    • Exclusion Constraints
    • Explicit Locks, Advisory Locks
  • Concurrency, Performance
    • Indexing: B-tree, Multicolumn, Expressions, Partial
    • Advanced Indexing: GiST, SP-Gist, KNN Gist, GIN, BRIN, Covering indexes, Bloom filters
    • Sophisticated query planner / optimizer, index-only scans, multicolumn statistics
    • Transactions, Nested Transactions (via savepoints)
    • Multi-Version concurrency Control (MVCC)
    • Parallelization of read queries and building B-tree indexes
    • Table partitioning
    • All transaction isolation levels defined in the SQL standard, including Serializable
    • Just-in-time (JIT) compilation of expressions
    • Asynchronous I/O (AIO)
  • Reliability, Disaster Recovery
    • Write-ahead Logging (WAL)
    • Replication: Asynchronous, Synchronous, Logical
    • Point-in-time-recovery (PITR), active standbys
    • Tablespaces
  • Security
    • Authentication: GSSAPI, SSPI, LDAP, SCRAM-SHA-256, Certificate, OAuth 2.0, and more
    • Robust access-control system
    • Column and row-level security
    • Multi-factor authentication with certificates and an additional method
  • Extensibility
    • Stored functions and procedures
    • Procedural Languages: PL/pgSQL, Perl, Python, and Tcl. There are other languages available through extensions, e.g. Java, JavaScript (V8), R, Lua, and Rust
    • SQL/JSON constructors, query functions, path expressions, and JSON_TABLE
    • Foreign data wrappers: connect to other databases or streams with a standard SQL interface
    • Customizable storage interface for tables
    • Many extensions that provide additional functionality, including PostGIS
  • Internationalisation, Text Search
    • Support for international character sets, e.g. through ICU collations
    • Case-insensitive and accent-insensitive collations
    • Full-text search

There are many more features that you can discover in the PostgreSQL documentation. Additionally, PostgreSQL is highly extensible: many features, such as indexes, have defined APIs so that you can build out with PostgreSQL to solve your challenges.

PostgreSQL has been proven to be highly scalable both in the sheer quantity of data it can manage and in the number of concurrent users it can accommodate. There are active PostgreSQL clusters in production environments that manage many terabytes of data, and specialized systems that manage petabytes.

Any questions?

The first place to go to for any questions on PostgreSQL is its world-renowned documentation, which discusses how to use PostgreSQL in-depth.

We also have many mailing lists where you can connect and participate in the community. There are also many events and local user groups where you can connect with other PostgreSQL users.

"We have used PostgreSQL successfully for over two years in a mission-critical capacity to support our registry systems."

The PostgreSQL Global Development Group has released an update to all supported versions of PostgreSQL, including 18.4, 17.10, 16.14, 15.18, and 14.23. This release fixes 11 security vulnerabilities and over 60 bugs reported over the last several months.

For the more information about this release, please review the release notes. You can download PostgreSQL from the download page.

PostgreSQL 14 will stop receiving fixes on November 12, 2026. If you are running PostgreSQL 14 in a production environment, we suggest that you make plans to upgrade to a newer, supported version of PostgreSQL. Please see our versioning policy for more information.
